fix(web): stop the tab highlight stretching when tabs load late

## Description

On first open of Instance Settings, the highlight behind the active tab stretched across several tabs until you clicked one. The tab bar measured the active tab before the qBittorrent tabs loaded, and nothing measured it again when they appeared. The shared tab bar now measures the highlight again when a tab button changes size, appears, or disappears, so every page that uses it gets the fix.

Fixes #4343

**Merge danger:** two-way door, blast radius: the highlight on every shared tab bar.

## Breaking change

No breaking change.

## Behaviour change

The highlight covers only the active tab on first open of Instance Settings, and on any tab bar whose tabs load or change size after it first draws.

## How has this been tested?

Before and after on two local builds (merge base and this branch) against a stub qBittorrent, in headless Chromium at 1440×900. Measured the highlight against the active tab after the qBittorrent tabs loaded:

| Build | Active tab width | Highlight width | Runs |
|---|---|---|---|
| merge base | 270 px | 501 px | 3/3 mismatch |
| this branch | 270 px | 270 px | 3/3 match |

On this branch the highlight also matched after a tab switch, after a resize from 1440 to 1000 px, and on the Dashboard 24 h / Live tabs. Both builds logged the same console errors from the rig, and the fix adds none.

Evidence: https://bin.getqui.com/e/TBXSIP3ZV4A5KLGZKI37NDYSXW

## Performance

No measurable cost. The new observers fire only when a tab button resizes or a tab is added or removed, and each callback reads the size of one tab, the same work as a tab click.

## Checklist

- [x] My PR title follows the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/#summary) format (it becomes the squashed commit message)
- [ ] If this changes the database schema, I have added migrations for both SQLite and PostgreSQL
- [x] I completed the [mandatory performance checks](https://github.com/autobrr/qui/blob/develop/docs/agents/performance-checks.md) and recorded the outcome in Performance

Reviewed with sol-loop: 1 round with gpt-6.2-sol. Sol verdict: approved

--- a/web/src/components/ui/tabs.tsx
+++ b/web/src/components/ui/tabs.tsx
@@ -46,19 +46,26 @@ function TabsList({
   }, [])
 
   React.useEffect(() => {
-    updateIndicator()
-
     const list = listRef.current
     if (!list) return
 
-    const observer = new MutationObserver(updateIndicator)
-    observer.observe(list, { attributes: true, subtree: true, attributeFilter: ["data-state"] })
-
     const resizeObserver = new ResizeObserver(updateIndicator)
-    resizeObserver.observe(list)
+    const observeTabs = () => {
+      resizeObserver.observe(list)
+      list.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>("[role=\"tab\"]").forEach(tab => resizeObserver.observe(tab))
+    }
+
+    const mutationObserver = new MutationObserver(() => {
+      observeTabs()
+      updateIndicator()
+    })
+    mutationObserver.observe(list, { attributes: true, attributeFilter: ["data-state"], childList: true, subtree: true })
+
+    observeTabs()
+    updateIndicator()
 
     return () => {
-      observer.disconnect()
+      mutationObserver.disconnect()
       resizeObserver.disconnect()
     }
   }, [updateIndicator])

fix(web): show library diagnostics numbers in the interface language's digits ## Problem Related issue: N/A Validation tasks: none. #198 and #1251 C1 use the Libraries page, but English output is unchanged. Other clients: Apple N/A (web admin only); Android N/A (web admin only); Roku N/A (web admin only) The admin Libraries page's diagnostics sections printed their numbers directly into the page instead of through `numberText()`. In an Arabic interface whose format locale uses Arabic-Indic digits, those numbers stayed in Latin digits while the page's dates and messages switched. This affected section header counts, Metadata Matcher pending and parked counts, Troubleshooting and Ambiguous Roots file counts, and Stale IDs years. `web/src/i18n/README.md` ("Digits") says a number shown outside a message goes through `numberText()`. The setup that shows it: a browser language of Arabic with Arabic-Indic digits, such as `ar-EG` or `ar-SA`. The interface resolves to Arabic, and the Arabic formatter takes the browser locale's numbering system. On a plain `ar` or `ar-AE` locale, Arabic uses Latin digits for dates as well, so nothing differs there. English and every other language are unchanged, because `numberText()` returns the plain number for them. ## Approach Each displayed number goes through `numberText()` at the place it is printed: the shared header count in `CollapsibleDiagnosticsSection`, and the counts and years in the Ambiguous Roots, Metadata Matcher, Troubleshooting (skipped roots) and Stale IDs sections. The candidate and raw-file years that the Matcher builds into display strings get the same treatment. The library editor's box-set minimum picker, in the same folder, had the same pattern and is included. React keys, comparisons, sort and filter values, and the `count === 0` styling still use the raw numbers. The Unmatched Items year and pager already pass numbers through messages and didn't need a change. This PR stays off the Ambiguous Roots badge lines that #4994 changes, so the two merge cleanly. No catalog keys change. ## Validation - Reproduced live: on a dev sandbox, Admin → Libraries in a Chromium context with locale `ar-EG` showed Latin `1`, `0` and `3` counts next to Arabic-Indic dates on `main`. With this change they show `١`, `٠` and `٣`, at desktop and phone widths. An `en-US` capture of the fix shows the page unchanged. - The sandbox has no ambiguous roots, stale IDs or parked entries. A scratch component render under `ar-EG` covered the Stale IDs year, the skipped-root file count, and the pending and parked counts. Seven of them fail on `main` too, and the rest pass when run alone with this change. Evidence: https://evidence.siloserver.org/r/silo-server/libraries-diagnostics-digits/ ## Risks None identified. The change is display-only. fix(web): keep a search result's title readable in the Editor's Picks title search

## Problem

Related issue: N/A
Validation tasks: none

Other clients: Apple N/A (no Home row editor); Android N/A (no Home row editor); Roku N/A (no Home row editor)

In the Home row editor, the Editor's Picks title search (reached through **Edit row** on an existing Editor's Picks row) shows each result as the title followed by "year · type", all in one span that is cut at its end and takes the page's direction. Three things go wrong:

- A long title in the other script loses its start. An Arabic title in an English page shows its last words, and an English title in a right-to-left page does the same.
- A cut title hides its year and type, which helps tell two titles with the same name apart.
- On a narrow row at a large text size, the year and type take width the title needs.

The review of #4983 and #5009 found this. The same row in the profile editor's allowed titles search had the same markup until #5009 fixed it.

## Approach

Each result row now matches #5009. The title sits on its own line with `dir="auto"` and `.bidi-text`, as `web/src/i18n/README.md` asks of cut titles from metadata, so it keeps its own start in either script. The year and type sit on a second line under it. That line is translated text (`web.home.addRow.curated.resultMeta`), so it keeps the page's direction and has no `dir="auto"`. The Add button and its labels don't change.

## Validation

- Before and after on a dev-only harness page (removed before commit) that rendered the real `CuratedTitlesEditor` with seeded results: a long English title, a long Arabic title, a short title, and a series with no year. Captured in headless Chromium at 320 px with the largest text size in a left-to-right and a right-to-left page, and at 400 px with the default text size.
  - Before: the year and type were cut off in every long row. The Arabic title in the English page and the English titles in the right-to-left page showed their end.
  - After: every title starts from its own start, and every row shows its year and type.
- Web `tsc -b`, `eslint`, and `prettier --check`: pass. No test renders this row.

Evidence: https://evidence.siloserver.org/r/silo-server/curated-titles-search-bidi/

## Risks

None identified. Result rows are a few pixels taller, so the scrolling list shows slightly fewer results at once.

fix(web): keep accents and vowel signs in provider monograms

## Problem

Related issue: N/A
Validation tasks: none

Other clients: N/A (web admin only; the provider tiles that show this mark exist only in the web admin)

When a provider has no logo, the web admin shows a two-letter mark built from its name (plugin tiles, marker providers, request servers, watch providers). `providerMonogram` removed every character that isn't a letter or digit before taking those two characters, and that also removed combining marks. A name spelled with a decomposed accent lost the accent: "e" + U+0301 + "clair" gave "EC" while the precomposed spelling gave "ÉC". A Devanagari name lost its vowel signs: "हिंदी" gave "हद".

Found in review of #4998. The defect was already on main before that PR.

## Approach

Split the name as written into characters with the same segmentation `leadingGraphemes` uses, and take the first two that contain a letter or digit. A letter keeps its accents and vowel signs, and two letters taken from different words get a zero width non-joiner between them, so a word-final virama can't fuse with the next word's letter into one conjunct. The non-joiner is invisible elsewhere. A keycap emoji such as 1️⃣ counts as its digit, as it did before. `web/src/lib/text.ts` now exports that segmentation as `graphemeClusters`, and `leadingGraphemes` uses it without changing what it returns. ASCII names come out the same ("AniList" is still "AN", an empty name is still "??").

In browsers without `Intl.Segmenter` (Firefox before 125), characters fall back to code points, so combining marks are skipped there as before.

## Validation

- New focused test `web/src/lib/monogram.test.ts`: fails on main 3a8bd2228c (decomposed "éclair" gives "EC", "हिंदी" gives "हद", "वाक् संवाद" gives "वक") and passes on this branch. Two more rows cover the review findings below. The avatar-initial tests in `text.test.ts` still pass.
- `tsc --noEmit` for the web app, eslint and prettier on the changed files, and `make lint-changed`: clean.
- Not reproduced on a live deployment: provider names come from plugins, and no installed plugin has such a name.

## Evidence

Evidence: https://evidence.siloserver.org/r/silo-server/provider-monogram-combining-marks/

fix(web): keep an unbreakable folder name off the start edge of right-to-left path lists ## Problem Related issue: #4935 Validation tasks: none Other clients: Apple N/A (web admin layout only); Android N/A (web admin layout only); Roku N/A (web admin layout only) Since #4979, a folder name that can't wrap, such as one long emoji sequence, runs past the start edge of two path lists when the web app is in Arabic or Hebrew: the backup restore Choose step's folder list and the library card paths on the Libraries page. On a phone it runs off the right side of the screen; on a wide screen it runs under the admin sidebar. This change makes it widen the list toward the page's end side instead, the mirror of English, as it did before #4979. Short and wrapped paths keep #4979's fix and still sit on the page's start side. The adversarial review of #4979 found this. #4979 replaced `w-fit` with `align-with-page` on those lists. Without `w-fit`, the list is as wide as its column, and a line too long for it is start-aligned in its own left-to-right direction, so it spills past the right edge. ## Approach Both lists keep `w-fit` beside `align-with-page`. `w-fit` sizes the list to its longest unbreakable name, so the overflow goes the page's end way; `align-with-page` still lines up each wrapped line. The `align-with-page` bullet in the i18n README now says what the class copies (the parent's `text-align`, with `start` and `end` resolved in the parent's direction), why Firefox and Safari hide the problem in list items (their `li` takes `text-align: match-parent`), and that a path block that would stretch also takes `w-fit` without `max-w-full`. The `PathText` bullet below it now sends wrapped paths to that rule instead of to the sizing for cut names. ## Validation - Checked on a dev-only fixture page that renders the real components (never committed), with a folder named by 30 emoji joined into one character cluster. A Silo deployment can't easily hold that folder, so it wasn't checked live. In Arabic at 393 px, the name ran 121 to 211 px past the start edge before, depending on the list and engine, and runs the same distance past the end edge after, in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit. English is unchanged. - #4979's alignment measurements rerun with this change: every line of a short or wrapped path still sits 0 to 1 px from the start edge in all three engines, in Arabic and English, at 360 to 1000 px, and no page scrolls sideways. - Web lint, typecheck and build, format check, and the local-path check pass. No test added: the overflow is layout, which jsdom doesn't compute. ## Evidence Evidence: https://evidence.siloserver.org/r/silo-server/rtl-path-list-overflow/ ## Risks None identified. The two lists go back to the width they had before #4979, which only differs when a name can't wrap. ## Checklist - [x] I read and can explain the complete diff. - [x] This pull request addresses one concern. - [x] Each test this pull request adds meets "Decide what to test" in CONTRIBUTING.md. - [x] The Evidence section shows every change a user can see, or how I checked a change nobody sees. ## Follow-ups - Folders named in Arabic swap places in these lists because they print the raw path instead of `PathText`: tracked in #4776, which also needs the matcher queue path and `CardPath`. ## Council review This PR fixes findings from #4979's adversarial review: S1 (this overflow), S2, G1 and G2 (the README wording). fix(client): a window wider than the GPU's texture limit still renders (#4028)

Fixes #4028

`renderer_failed` reports from players whose window is wider than the GPU's texture limit (4 since 11-11), e.g. `Invalid surface size. Backing surface has size (8820, 5226) but attempting to configure a size of (8192, 5226)`. The canvas backing store was the CSS box × `devicePixelRatio` with no bound.

## Change
- `video-options.ts`: `SURFACE_MAX_DIMENSION` (8192: WebGPU's default `maxTextureDimension2D`; `device.ts` requests no limits, so every device has exactly this) and `surfaceSize(w, h)`, which scales an oversized store down whole with the aspect ratio kept.
- `platform.ts` `readViewport` applies it, and records `surfacePixelRatio` (backing pixels per CSS pixel). `displayScale` (pointer mapping) and `uiPixelScale` read that instead of `devicePixelRatio`, so a click lands where the clamped frame drew. Unclamped, it equals `devicePixelRatio`: no change for any window under 8192 pixels.

Native: not a native rule (the original has no WebGPU surface); this only keeps the port's renderer alive.

Old-tab: safe - client-only change; no wire, data or asset contract changes.

## What ran
- `pnpm run verify:quick` (typecheck, ownership, capabilities, execution map): exit 0.
- `node --test tests/runtime/video-options.test.mjs tests/runtime/title-tiny-viewport.test.mjs tests/runtime/render-scale-surface.test.mjs tests/architecture/ownership.test.mjs`: 42 pass, 0 fail. The new test covers the reported 8820×5226 window, a tall window, and the unchanged sizes.
- `node scripts/checks/check_formatting.mjs`: no new unformatted files.

## Four questions
- **Is it SRP?** Yes: `surfaceSize` only bounds a size; the platform, which owns the viewport, applies it once.
- **Is it DRY? (rg.exe)** Yes: `rg -n "maxTextureDimension2D|surfaceSize|devicePixelRatio" apps/client-next/src`: there was no clamp anywhere; the viewport is computed in one place and every reader (renderer, UI scale, pointer) gets that one size.
- **Is it scalable?** Yes: a bound with no per-frame cost beyond one division, and it holds for any display size.
- **Are the ownership of the code correct?** Yes: the platform owns the canvas size and pointer mapping; the limit sits next to the other viewport geometry in `video-options.ts`, with the device's default limits cited.

fix(build): an avatar effect is checked against the equipment records, not the caller's dress (#4013)

Fixes #4013

This is a release blocker for r203r. The build at freeze 440e7084d stopped in its client check: four particle tests threw `Avatar effect for a non-avatar item 24357`.

#4008 checked each avatar effect against `dress.equipment[id].avatarSlot`, which is the dress the caller hands in. The tests hand in a one-item dress. With the default data no mall-avatar marker is enabled, so CI never ran the check. The release variant enables the marker (64 avatar effects), and the check threw.

`avatarSlot` is built from the equipment record's `avatar` flag (`buildEquipmentVisuals.mjs:301`). So the check now lives in `avatarWornEffects`, against that record, and refuses a marker naming a non-avatar item whichever dress asks. All 64 variant items are avatars in the records.

## Four questions

- **Is it SRP?** Yes. `avatarWornEffects` reads and validates the marker. The publisher only attaches the result.
- **Is it DRY? (rg.exe)** Yes. `rg -n "avatarSlot|non-avatar" scripts/build`: the flag has one source (`row.avatar`), and the check now exists once.
- **Is it scalable?** Yes. One lookup per marker row, on records already loaded.
- **Are the ownership of the code correct?** Yes. The equipment records own what an avatar is, and the check reads them rather than a caller's partial dress.

## What ran

- `node --test` for avatar-worn-effects, compound-sockets, enchant-sparks and equipment-particles:
  - default data: 17 passed;
  - release variant roots (`SRO_GAME_ROOT`/`SRO_GENERATED_ROOT` = the r203r staging): 16 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped by design (native census).
- Without the record check, the new assertion fails (exit 1).
- `dprint check` on both files: exit 0. `check_source_encoding.mjs`: exit 0.

fix(web): keep a media title's start in the admin subtitles table ## Problem Related issue: N/A Validation tasks: none Other clients: N/A (web admin page with no counterpart in the Apple, Android, or Roku apps) In a right-to-left language such as Arabic, the Media column of Admin → Subtitle Files showed a long Latin title without its start and without a "…". A title that starts with digits read out of order: "13 Hours: The Secret Soldiers of Benghazi" showed as "…Secret Soldiers of Benghazi 13". In English, long titles were clipped mid-letter. The same titles read correctly in marker history. The cell applies `whitespace-nowrap`, so the title's `line-clamp-2` never wrapped. The text overflowed the 220px cell and was clipped on its overflow side, which in a right-to-left page is the start. This change cuts the title to one line, keeps its start and its "…" in every language, and shows the full title on hover. Found in review of #4984. ## Approach The title takes `.bidi-text`, `dir="auto"`, and `truncate`, as `web/src/i18n/README.md` → "Right to left" asks for a cut title from metadata. The cell keeps its `max-w`. The release name and format chip cells that #4984 changes are untouched. Letting the title wrap to two lines, as `line-clamp-2` intended, doesn't work in Chromium: a clamped left-to-right block aligned to the right, where it has to sit on an Arabic page, loses its "…". Firefox and WebKit keep it. One line works in all three, matches marker history, and keeps English row heights as they are. ## Validation - Reproduced on a Silo dev deployment built from `main`, in Arabic, in Chromium. Also checked at phone width. - English, same page and data: the Media cell has the same width and row height before and after in all three engines. The only visible change is the "…" on a cut title. - `pnpm run lint` (no errors), `pnpm run format:check`, `tsc --noEmit`, `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run budget:check`, and the admin subtitles Vitest files pass. No browser console errors. ## Evidence Evidence: https://evidence.siloserver.org/r/silo-server/rtl-subtitles-media-title/ ## Risks None identified.
